course_name_original: Introducción al Diseño de Motores Eléctricos
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of rotating electrical machines

learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate theoretical knowledge about the constructive characteristics of different types of electric motors.

Know the properties of conductive materials used in the manufacture of electric motors and be able to select them appropriately and perform their dimensioning based on the power of the motor to be designed.

Know the properties of insulating materials used in the manufacture of electric motors and be able to select them appropriately based on the voltage and power characteristics of the motor to be designed.

Know the properties of magnetic materials used in the manufacture of the stator and rotor cores of electric motors and be able to select the appropriate product for the characteristics of the motor to be designed.
Know and identify the special properties and characteristics of the electromechanical structure of the rotor and stator magnetic cores of electric motors.
Know the most common types of stator windings used in electric motors and be able to design single and double-layer lap and wave windings.
Know and differentiate the different manufacturing technologies for electric motor rotors, selecting the most appropriate for the motor to be designed.
Identify the design variables of different types of electric motors, their interrelationship and limitations.
Know the criteria and limitations imposed by the design of stator and rotor magnetic cores. Be able to appropriately dimension yokes and slots based on the type of motor to be designed.
Be able to select and adapt the design of magnetic cores to standardized enclosures for low voltage asynchronous motors.
Be able to design a rotor cage for an asynchronous motor including the dimensioning, number, and cross-section of bars and rings based on the type of motor to be designed.
Formulate the basic equations that define the design of electric motors.
Know the simplified algebraic equations that allow a general dimensioning of an electric motor. Apply them for the initial dimensioning of the motor to be designed.
Be able to design the stator winding of an asynchronous motor including the dimensioning, number, and cross-section of the slots as well as the conductors housed within them.
Know and be able to apply simplified industrial methods for estimating rotor and stator leakage reactances based on the geometry of the motor to be designed.
Demonstrate skills in the use of specific computer tools for electric motor design.
Know the fundamentals of industrial electric motor design using commercial finite element calculation tools.
Be able to perform a two-dimensional cross-section design of a squirrel cage asynchronous motor using industrial numerical calculation software via the finite element method.

Be able to perform the complete design of a squirrel cage asynchronous motor using industrial analytical calculation software, evaluating the influence of varying the design parameters of its windings and magnetic cores on the motor's behavior.
Document the design project of an electric motor.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability for the calculation and design of electrical machines.
Knowledge about the control of electrical machines and drives and their applications.

teaching_methods: Construction of a motor with its sensorless inverter
Optional visits to motor repair and construction workshops

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment: complete construction of a 3D printed motor (assembly, winding, operation, measurements)
Laboratory practices evaluation (real equipment, simulation, questionnaires)
Mixed electric motor design project (analytical/computational using Ansys Electronics Desktop/Maxwell-RMXPRT)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, continuous assessment accounts for 2 points, laboratory practices for 4 points, and the mixed design project for 4 points. In the extraordinary call, if the student has achieved at least 50% in continuous assessment and laboratory practices, they can take a 2-hour analytical design exam, needing a total score >= 5 with at least 2 points in the exam. If not, the student must take the same analytical design exam (evaluated out of 5 points, min 2 points) and submit a software design verification (evaluated out of 5 points, min 2 points), needing a total score >= 5. For differentiated evaluation, students can choose between two in-person sessions with a theoretical analytical design exam using a summary of expressions, or completing the conventional assessment work and practical exam.
